lastCompletedStory.title: WARNING: The suite gate produces NO output for its entire ~101s run, contradict…

nextStoryContext: US-R2-001 fixed the round-2 WARNING finding: the suite ('test') gate's spawnFn was a Bun.spawnSync call with piped stdio -- fully synchronous, so it blocked in total silence for the whole ~101s+ run and only echoed the captured buffers back to the operator (captureAndEchoSuiteOutput) AFTER spawnFn returned. That contradicted US-001's own AC2 prose, this file's own header/inline comments, and ADR-0056's stated consequence ('the operator's live progress must be teed rather than swallowed') -- a post-hoc replay, not a tee. Root-cause fix chosen on merit over the alternative (accepting the replay and merely correcting the comments/ADR): scripts/check-all.ts's suite-gate spawn is now a genuine streaming tee. New exported helpers: `teeStream(stream, sink)` reads a ReadableStream<Uint8Array> chunk-by-chunk via `for await`, writing each chunk straight through to `sink` AS IT ARRIVES while accumulating every chunk into the returned combined Buffer; `runStreamingSuiteGate(cmd, args, cwd)` spawns via async Bun.spawn (stdout/stderr both 'pipe'), runs `teeStream` against process.stdout/process.stderr concurrently with `proc.exited` via Promise.all, and returns a SyncSubprocess-shaped result (pid/stdout/stderr/exitCode/success/resourceUsage/signalCode) so the rest of the pipeline is unchanged in shape. `makeDefaultSpawnFn` now dispatches to `runStreamingSuiteGate` only for the suite gate (same cmd==='bun'&&args[0]==='test'&&args.includes('--coverage') match as before) and keeps Bun.spawnSync+inherited-stdio for every other gate. Because streaming requires awaiting incremental reads, `SpawnFn` is now ALWAYS async (`Promise<SyncSubprocess<'pipe'|'inherit','pipe'|'inherit'>>`), which ripples through `runGates` (now `async function... : Promise<number>`), `runSpawnGate` (awaits spawnFn, no longer echoes -- echoing is now the real spawnFn's own job, `decodeCapturedOutput` is all this layer does), `executeGate` (async dispatcher), and the CLI entrypoint (`await runGates(...)`). `captureAndEchoSuiteOutput` was deleted (its job moved into runStreamingSuiteGate/teeStream); tests that stood in for it are unaffected since fake spawnFns never echoed for real anyway. Removed `withSilentStdio` from test/check-all-inprocess-gates.test.ts: it existed solely to silence the now-deleted post-hoc echo of fabricated 'Ran N tests.../N pass/All files' blobs (the exact self-hosting contamination hazard the old code path created); with the echo gone, fake spawn results in unit tests never write to real stdout at all, so the wrapper had zero remaining purpose (and would have been actively broken had it been left in place, since its `finally` restore fires synchronously before the now-async runGates call's internal awaits resolve). All three existing check-all test files were mechanically converted to async (fn: SpawnFn -> async, test callbacks -> async, runGates(...) calls -> await runGates(...)); no assertions changed. Added a NEW test/check-all-streaming.test.ts that proves the tee is real (not just type-correct) using a REAL Bun.spawn subprocess and REAL wall-clock timing (no fakes): `sh -c 'echo EARLY; sleep 0.4; echo LATE'` piped through `teeStream` must deliver the EARLY chunk to the sink well before the 400ms sleep completes and the LATE chunk only after -- the exact measurement class the original finding itself used (its own probe: `echo EARLY; sleep 3; echo LATE` unblocking only after ~3018ms under spawnSync). A second test drives `runStreamingSuiteGate` end-to-end with a real subprocess (stdout/stderr writes stubbed+captured, not suppressed) proving exitCode/success/stdout/stderr reflect the real child AND that the echo genuinely happened live via the production code path, not replayed by the test. ADR-0056 needed NO edit: its consequence sentence ('the operator's live progress must be teed rather than swallowed') is now simply TRUE, since this story implements the tee it was describing as the destination rather than the shipped shape -- no supersession note was needed because reality now matches the ADR's own stated consequence. scripts/check-all.ts's file-size ceiling raised 378->452 (actual gate-measured line count) with a dated _ref note prepended and staged before the file-size gate was re-run, per the CAM-488 story rubric. Full spine verified green: bun run typecheck (0 errors), bun test (5956 pass / 0 fail, +3 from the new streaming test file), bun run check:all (exit 0, all 14 gates ok including the newly-restated file-size ceiling). No more round-2 findings remain in prd.json as of this write; supervisor should proceed past round-2 review remediation.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed against current Bun docs: Bun.spawn's stdout/stderr default (and when explicitly 'pipe') resolve to ReadableStream<Uint8Array>, readable incrementally while the child is still running; Bun.spawnSync is documented verbatim as 'the blocking equivalent of Bun.spawn' (the exact defect this story fixes); Subprocess.resourceUsage() is documented as 'only available after the process has exited', matching this story's `proc.resourceUsage() ?? emptyResourceUsage()` fallback (read only after `await proc.exited` resolves, so the fallback branch is defensive, not expected to fire). Implementation (teeStream/runStreamingSuiteGate in scripts/check-all.ts) matches this shape exactly: no drift found.
